climate_admin.intro: Map the two climate zones onto this apartment's own Shelly devices - only device ids change between installs, nothing else. Changes here need a LocalHome restart to take effect.
climate_admin.broker_note: Edited by hand in config/mqtt_broker.json, not through this page - see docs/integrations/mqtt.md.
climate_admin.broker_down_hint: check that mosquitto is actually running on that host - if it is, every zone below will keep saying "not reachable" no matter what's changed on the device side.
climate_admin.broker_optional: optional - blank for an anonymous broker
climate_admin.broker_save_success: Saved - restart LocalHome for every device to reconnect through it.
climate_admin.zones_note: Exactly two zones. Pick a sensor source per zone: a real Shelly device, a simulated one (no hardware installed yet), or a manual value for debugging the control logic. Pick a valve source too - real, or simulated so it can still be tested (including with the manual open/close buttons below) before any relay is wired. Switching either source away from "Shelly" only stops LocalHome from talking to that device - it never sends anything to the real one. Each card's status below reflects whichever mapping is currently running (since the last restart), not unsaved edits above it - a card that says "saved, but not running yet" needs a restart before its status means anything.
climate_admin.manual_mode_hint: After saving and restarting, set the actual value from the Live status section below, next to this zone.
climate_admin.cool_enabled_label: Can be cooled (uncheck for a condensation-prone zone)
climate_admin.save_success: Saved - restart LocalHome, then reload this page to verify.
climate_admin.mode_formula_heat: valves open below target, close above it
climate_admin.mode_formula_cool: valves open above target, close below it
climate_admin.zone_excluded_cool: Excluded from cooling ("Can be cooled" is off for this zone) - the thermostat doesn't touch this valve for temperature while cooling. Whatever state it's in below is either idle or driven by an interlock, not this zone's own control loop.
climate_admin.restart_pending: Saved, but not running yet - restart LocalHome and reload this page to see it live.
climate_admin.restart_confirm: Restart LocalHome now? It'll be back in a few seconds, but nothing here will respond until it is.
climate_admin.restart_in_progress: Restarting - this page will reload itself once it's back.
climate_admin.restart_unsupported_windows: Restarting from the browser isn't reliable on Windows - it can leave two processes fighting over the same port instead of actually restarting. Stop the process yourself (Ctrl+C in its terminal) and start it again, then reload this page - fine for developing on Windows, this is a non-issue on the Linux box you'd actually deploy to.
climate_admin.restart_timeout: Still not responding after 30 seconds - check the terminal LocalHome is running in for an error, then reload this page by hand.
climate_admin.updated_ago_normal_cadence: {time} ago - normal, this sensor reports on a change or roughly every 2h
climate_admin.not_reachable_battery: Not reachable yet - battery sensors only report on their own wake cycle or a button press. Press the button on the device for an immediate test report.
climate_admin.not_reachable_offline: Was reporting, now unreachable - check the device is powered and in range.
climate_admin.valve_not_reachable: Not reachable - check the device id and that it's powered and connected to the broker.
climate_admin.valve_test_hint: Manual test - the thermostat takes back control on its next cycle.
climate_admin.manual_no_value: No manual value set yet - enter one below.
climate_admin.extra_switches_note: Two more fixed, standalone Shelly Plus 1 on/off switches, not tied to a zone and with no sensor - leave either blank if not wired yet. If config.yaml's thermostat.interlocks/mode_switches already control one of these by a different name, update that config.yaml entry to say "Bathroom Bypass Valve"/"Dehumidifier" instead - this panel always uses those exact names.
climate_admin.extra_sensor_note: One more fixed, standalone Shelly H&T Gen3 sensor - outdoor temperature/humidity, not tied to any zone. Always a real device (no simulated/manual mode, unlike a zone's own sensor) - leave blank if not wired yet.
climate_admin.how_it_works_heading: How this works - sensors, thresholds and edge cases
climate_admin.how_it_works_threshold: A battery sensor (Shelly H&T Gen3) only sends a new reading when its temperature moves by at least 0.5°C or its humidity by at least 5% - or every 2 hours regardless, even if nothing changed at all. So a zone that sits at a rock-stable temperature for hours, with its reading's age creeping up toward 2h, is completely normal, not a fault - the 2h heartbeat is what keeps it "Reporting" instead of ever needing to be treated as stale just from being stable (confirmed with an overnight watch of two real sensors: every heartbeat landed within about a minute of exactly 2h). Only a reading whose age passes stale_after_seconds (4h - just under double the heartbeat, so one missed heartbeat alone never trips it, but two in a row does) is treated as actually unreachable.
climate_admin.how_it_works_wifi: A zone card's WiFi signal figure (shown next to its reading, when reported) below "fair" means the sensor is spending more of its battery retrying its connection, not just reporting slower - moving it closer to the broker's access point, or adding a repeater, fixes battery drain that a firmware update or a config change here cannot.
climate_admin.how_it_works_battery: Battery percentage is shown inline with each zone's reading, highlighted once it's at or below 10% - the same threshold the main dashboard's own low-battery popup uses. Replacing the batteries clears it on the sensor's next report; there's nothing to reset here.
climate_admin.how_it_works_failsafe: If a zone's sensor stays unreachable (not just quiet - actually unreachable, see above) for longer than its failsafe threshold (24h by default), its valve is forced closed automatically rather than left frozen in whatever it was doing indefinitely - shown on that zone's card below as it approaches and crosses the threshold. It clears itself the moment the sensor reports again. To open that valve anyway before the sensor comes back (e.g. while replacing its battery), use Diagnostic mode below.
climate_admin.how_it_works_diagnostic: Diagnostic mode (below) is the way to move any valve by hand regardless of what any sensor says - for verifying a relay actually switches, figuring out which physical valve is which name, or riding out a sensor failsafe or an extended away period without waiting.
climate_admin.diagnostic_note: Takes command over every valve this apartment has - both zones' valves and the two extra switches (bathroom bypass, dehumidifier), whichever are currently wired. While on, the thermostat and every interlock/mode switch stop touching any of them entirely, not even to force a safe state - each valve stays exactly where you (or its last real command before this turned on) left it, moved only by the buttons below. Turning it back off resumes normal sensor-driven control immediately, no restart needed.
climate_admin.diagnostic_active_banner: Diagnostic mode is ON - the thermostat and all interlocks are hands-off. Every valve below only moves when you press its button.
climate_admin.diagnostic_confirm_on: Turn on diagnostic mode? The thermostat and all interlocks will stop controlling every valve until you turn this back off.
climate_admin.failsafe_active: Failsafe active: this sensor has been unreachable for {hours}h, past its threshold - its valve has been forced closed automatically. It will resume normal control the moment the sensor reports again, or use Diagnostic mode above to open it sooner.
climate_admin.failsafe_pending: Sensor unreachable for {hours}h - its valve stays as it was for now; it'll be forced closed automatically at {threshold}h unless the sensor recovers first.
climate_admin.system_note: The state of the installation itself rather than of one zone: what didn't load and why, which devices aren't responding, whether the control and recording loops are running, and the process, disk and history numbers that tell a slow problem (memory growing, disk filling up) apart from normal. Refreshed every 15 seconds.
climate_admin.system_problem_loop_stalled: {subject} loop stalled - check the service logs
climate_admin.system_skipped_note: Expected if you don't use those devices. If you did configure one, it's also listed under problems, and installs with the command shown.
climate_admin.system_skipped_line: package {package} is missing, install it with
climate_admin.vmc_note: The mechanical ventilation, driven by a Shelly 0/1-10V Dimmer Gen3: one device id builds its on/off switch and speed slider, shown on the dashboard. Leave blank if not wired yet.
climate_admin.vmc_suggestion: Found in config.yaml ("{name}"). Save to manage it from here: after the restart the config.yaml entry for this device is ignored and the VMC shows up as "VMC".
climate_admin.vmc_offline_hint: mains-powered device: check the id, that it's powered and connected to the MQTT broker.
